summary: Frontend-only E2E test of the timezone-aware (instant-based) schedule feature in OfficeFlow. Logged in as admin@example.com, switched the display timezone via the top-bar Timezone menu (Asia/Dhaka, America/Los_Angeles, Asia/Tokyo, UTC) and verified the Dispatch > Schedules table, the Dispatch > Calendar, and the create-shift flow. 6 of 7 requested scenarios PASS. One CRITICAL failure found: the Dispatch Calendar month grid places shifts on the WRONG day cell (and shows the wrong month label) whenever the display timezone differs from the browser timezone - the exact scenario the feature was built for.

ui_bugs.issue: With display timezone = America/Los_Angeles (browser zone UTC), the month header reads 'May 2026' while the grid actually renders June 2026, and every day-cell's data-testid is one day behind the day number it displays. Result: the seeded shift (backend date 2026-06-01 in LA) is rendered in the cell that visually shows '2' instead of Jun 1, and the newly created Jun-10 LA shift is rendered in the cell that visually shows '11'. With Asia/Dhaka (positive offset vs UTC browser) the same page is correct (header 'June 2026', shift on cell showing '2' = 2026-06-02, and on '10'). This FAILS the requested check 'Calendar with timezone Los Angeles must show the shift on Jun 1, not Jun 2'.
The status Select ('Not Started') is visually clipped/overlapped by the sticky right-hand MANAGE column, rendering as 'Not Start'. Reproduced at 1920x1080 in every timezone.

Navigating to a non-existent dashboard route (e.g. /dashboard/dispatch/schedule - singular, an easy typo since the real route is /schedules) renders a completely blank white page with no 404 message or redirect.

Date and Start/End Time fields use native browser <input type=date>/<input type=time> pickers rather than the shadcn Calendar/time components used elsewhere in the design system (locale-dependent display: shows 06/10/2026 and 09:00 AM while the table renders 24h / '10 Jun 2026').

integration_issues.flow: Account-saved display timezone adoption on fresh login
integration_issues.issue: FLAKY (1 of 2 fresh sessions): after logging in on a browser with no localStorage override, the app rendered everything in the browser zone (UTC) even though GET /api/auth/me returned timezone 'Asia/Dhaka'; a later session with the same setup correctly adopted the account zone (GMT+9). Likely RCA: TimezoneContext mutates a module-level ACTIVE_TZ and only triggers the corrective window.location.reload() when sessionStorage 'tz_synced' is unset, so any session where that key already exists (or where the effect runs after the first data fetches) keeps sending the wrong X-Timezone header for the whole page load. PUT /auth/me/timezone itself persists correctly (verified auth/me returned Asia/Tokyo after switching).

issues: Shift-status badge truncated behind the sticky MANAGE column
'DUTY HOURS' header wraps awkwardly to 'DUTY HOUR / S' in the narrow column
Month title label disagrees with the rendered grid when display timezone != browser timezone (shows 'May 2026' over a June grid)

action_items: FIX (HIGH): /app/frontend/src/pages/dashboard/dispatch/DispatchCalendarPage.js - iso(d) uses dhakaDateIso(d) which formats a browser-local Date in the ACTIVE display timezone, shifting the key by a day whenever the display zone is behind the browser zone. Build the ISO key from the Date's own local components instead (`${d.getFullYear()}-${pad(d.getMonth()+1)}-${pad(d.getDate())}`) for: the month/week/day grid cell keys (line ~514), the range.from/range.to sent as date_from/date_to (lines ~74-91, which also currently query 2026-05-31..2026-06-29 instead of the full month), and `today` (todayIso, line ~499).

FIX (HIGH): DispatchCalendarPage line ~190 - `label = formatMonth(cursor)` converts the browser-local cursor into the display zone and reports the previous month. Format the cursor's local month directly.

FIX (MEDIUM): TimezoneContext.js - make the account-timezone adoption deterministic before the first API calls (e.g. resolve the zone during auth bootstrap instead of a post-mount effect + one-shot sessionStorage-guarded reload) so X-Timezone is always correct on the first render.
FIX (LOW): give the shift-status column enough width / z-index so it is not covered by the sticky MANAGE column.
FIX (LOW): add a 404 route for unknown /dashboard/* paths instead of a blank page.
NOTE: add explicit data-testid attributes to the start/end time cells (currently only the wrapper `cell-start_time-<id>` exists) to make timezone regressions easier to assert.
critical_code_review_comments: datetime.js formats Date objects (whose components are browser-local) in ACTIVE_TZ. This is correct for real instants (ISO strings from the API) but WRONG for locally constructed 'calendar' Dates such as the calendar cursor/grid cells - that is the root cause of the calendar off-by-one-day bug. Consider separating 'instant formatters' from 'local calendar helpers' and never passing a locally-built Date through dhakaDateIso/formatMonth.
DispatchCalendarPage.js is 818 lines; the month/week/day grids should be split into separate components.

TimezoneContext.setPreference() fires api.put('/auth/me/timezone') and then calls window.location.reload() synchronously; the in-flight request can be aborted by the navigation. It happened to persist in testing, but the write should be awaited (or sent via keepalive) before reloading.
TimezoneMenu options are hardcoded in the context; the auto-detected zone is not shown as a selectable/checked entry when it is outside TIMEZONE_OPTIONS.
seed_data_creation: Created one dispatch schedule via the UI: Acme Corp / Guard Vendor / Main Gate (P100) / John Officer, date 2026-06-10, 09:00-17:00 entered while display timezone was America/Los_Angeles (stored instant = 2026-06-10T16:00Z). It is still present in the DB and is used by the cross-timezone assertions.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified PASS: (1) Schedules table conversion of the seeded shift - Asia/Dhaka 02 Jun 2026 08:00-16:00; America/Los_Angeles 01 Jun 2026 19:00-03:00; Asia/Tokyo 02 Jun 2026 11:00-19:00; UTC 02 Jun 2026 02:00-10:00. (2) Timezone menu switch + reload + localStorage 'officeflow_tz_pref' + PUT /auth/me/timezone persistence (auth/me reflected Asia/Tokyo). (3) Create shift from the LA view (2026-06-10 09:00-17:00) -> LA shows Wed 10 Jun 09:00-17:00, Asia/Dhaka shows Wed 10 Jun 22:00-06:00, Asia/Tokyo shows Thu 11 Jun 01:00-09:00 - fully instant-based, date shifts correctly. Verified FAIL: Dispatch Calendar month grid day placement + month label when display tz != browser tz (container browser tz is UTC). Real routes are /dashboard/dispatch/schedules and /dashboard/dispatch/calendar (NOT /schedule). Calendar defaults to Week view anchored on today (Aug 2026) - switch [data-testid=calendar-view-select] to Month then click [data-testid=cal-prev] twice to reach June 2026. Still untested: client portal schedule view (no credentials), week/day calendar views, Wage Report / Invoices / Excel export timezone handling, DST boundary dates.
rca_of_the_issue: DispatchCalendarPage.js defines `iso(d) => dhakaDateIso(d)`, and dhakaDateIso does `d.toLocaleDateString('en-CA', { timeZone: ACTIVE_TZ })`. The grid cell Dates and the cursor are created with browser-local constructors (`new Date(y, m, 1)`, `setDate()`), i.e. midnight in the BROWSER zone. Re-formatting that instant in a display zone that is behind the browser zone (UTC browser + America/Los_Angeles display = -7h) rolls it back to the previous calendar day. Consequently: (a) `data-testid={cal-cell-${iso(d)}}` and the byDate[r.date] lookup key are one day behind the `{d.getDate()}` number actually rendered, so a shift whose viewer-local date is 2026-06-01 lands in the cell that displays '2'; (b) `formatMonth(cursor)` prints 'May 2026' for a June cursor; (c) `range.from/to` sent as date_from/date_to are also shifted (2026-05-31 -> 2026-06-29 for June), so the last day of a month can be silently missing from the calendar. The schedules TABLE is unaffected because it renders the backend-localised plain strings r.date/r.start_time/r.end_time and never re-converts them. Fix: derive ISO keys from the Date's own local getFullYear/getMonth/getDate components (and format the month label from those components) rather than routing locally constructed Dates through the display-zone formatters.
